vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw360
Version: 0.1.6

The openclaw360 skill is a security framework for AI agents, providing features like prompt injection detection, sensitive data masking (DLP), and static analysis of other skills (scan-skills). It follows security best practices by using pinned git commits for installation, requiring user confirmation for initialization, and performing all operations locally without data exfiltration. The requested permissions to read skill directories and write to its own configuration folder (~/.openclaw360/) are strictly aligned with its documented purpose as a security auditing and runtime protection tool.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are internally consistent with a local security-scanner helper; nothing requested is disproportionate to that purpose, but the user should review the GitHub code before running the pip install and confirm creation/storage of local keys.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (runtime security: prompt-injection detection, tool-call authorization, DLP, skill scanning) align with the declared needs: only python3 and a per-skill config directory (~/.openclaw360/) and read access to target Skill directories. No unrelated cloud credentials, system-level files, or surprising binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions confine operations to local commands and to reading SKILL.md and script files in user-specified skill directories and ~/.openclaw360/ audit/config. This is appropriate for a scanner, but scan-skills will read arbitrary files the user points it at (including scripts that might contain secrets) — the SKILL.md says it won't touch ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config etc., which is good but relies on user-specified paths. Also the SKILL.md uses default scan paths (~/.openclaw/skills/) that differ from the skill's config directory (~/.openclaw360/), which looks like a naming/typo mismatch to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and provides pip install commands that fetch a pinned commit via git+https from GitHub. Using a pinned commit is better than an unpinned install, but pip installing directly from a repo executes remote code during install — the SKILL.md states the user runs these commands manually. This is a reasonable install method for a Python CLI tool, but users should inspect the referenced commit before running and prefer a venv.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. The only declared config paths are inside ~/.openclaw360/ (config.json, identity keys, audit logs). Generating and storing an Ed25519 identity key locally is consistent with claimed signing/audit functions; the SKILL.md states user confirmation is required before creation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: disable-model-invocation is set true and always is false: the skill will not be autonomously or globally forced into agent runs. It does not request system-wide configuration changes or permanent elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for a local security-scanner helper. Before installing: (1) review the exact GitHub commit referenced by the pip command to verify there is no unexpected network/telemetry behavior; (2) install inside a Python virtualenv (the SKILL.md provides a venv command) rather than system Python; (3) confirm and protect the created ~/.openclaw360/identity/ key material (it is used for local signing); (4) when using scan-skills, point it only at directories you trust — it will read scripts and SKILL.md files you provide and may encounter files that contain secrets; and (5) note the small naming mismatch (~/.openclaw/skills/ vs ~/.openclaw360/) and verify paths used at runtime. Because model invocation is disabled, the agent will not call this skill autonomously, lowering risk.
